items.title: release.yml's two `gate` legs run the WHOLE suite unsharded on one runner each — gate (windows) 110 min and gate (ubuntu) 55 min of a 2 h 1 min release run at v0.45.0, with every build and publish job (<= 9 min each) waiting on them; shard them as ci.yml does (ubuntu 2, windows 4) and route the ubuntu shards to the self-hosted runner
items.body: At v0.45.0 (run 37806603753) the release took 2 h 1 min: gate (windows-latest) 110 min, gate (ubuntu-latest) 55 min, clippy/fmt/audit/vsix/wasm 0-2 min, the five builds 3-9 min, the five publishes 0 min - everything downstream of `gate`. ci.yml's suite legs already run as `count:N/M` shards (ubuntu 2, windows 4) with the trusted ubuntu shards on the owner's `vilan-linux` runner, and the same tree was green there minutes earlier. Fix: the gate job takes ci.yml's `include` matrix (`VILAN_CI_PARTITION`), its doc-test step on partition 1 only, and the same `runs-on` routing (a tag push is a push, so it is trusted); the publish jobs stay GitHub-hosted (secrets). Expected: the gate's critical path 110 -> ~35 min (less once a windows runner exists, L24). The release's own gate still stands between the tag and the publish; it is not replaced by ci's verdict. Keep the `ci_local_script` pin that holds release.yml's gate and ci.yml's test leg to the same script.

items.title: a native WINDOWS self-hosted runner on the WSL host (`vilan-windows`) takes the trusted windows legs — ci.yml's four test shards and release.yml's windows gate (110 min at v0.45.0) and windows build — with the same fork gating as the Linux runner
items.body: The Linux runner (Docker, label `vilan-linux`, proposals/scripts/integration/runner/) proved out over Order 48: ubuntu shards 10-19 min against 44-56 on GitHub's, a CI run 35 min from 67. The windows legs are now the long pole everywhere (ci: 16-34 min per shard; release: the 110-min gate). A native runner on the Windows host of this WSL VM: the GitHub runner installed as a Windows service, label `vilan-windows`, with rustup (stable + the pinned 1.98.1 with rustfmt/clippy), Node 24, Git, the VS Build Tools (MSVC) and Python 3.12; ci.yml's `runs-on` picks `vilan-windows` for trusted windows legs the way it picks `vilan-linux` (`needs.changes.outputs.trusted`); release.yml the same for its windows gate and build. NOT self-hosted: the macOS builds (Apple hardware), the linux-arm build (GitHub's arm runner beats QEMU), perf (its ceilings are the hosted runners'), every publish job (secrets). Caps: the Windows service shares the host with the WSL VM's 30 GB; size the VM and the runner so a windows shard and a lane build can coexist. Deliverables: a PowerShell install script + README beside the Linux runner's, the routing patch; the owner registers the runner (Settings > Actions > Runners > New > Windows).
